name: BEZIQUE
description: Bezique is the aristocratic ancestor of Pinochle, a trick-taking and melding game for two players. Historically favored by Winston Churchill, it is played with a 64-card deck (two 32-card decks stripped). Players score points by declaring melds like 'Bezique' (Queen of Spades + Jack of Diamonds) and 'Royal Marriage' (King + Queen of Trumps) after winning tricks. The game is a race to 1000 points, characterized by a unique 'Trick-and-Draw' phase where hands are constantly refilled.

content.text: Bezique is the aristocratic ancestor of Pinochle, a trick-taking and melding game for two players. Historically favored by Winston Churchill, it is played with a 64-card deck (two 32-card decks stripped). Players score points by declaring melds like 'Bezique' (Queen of Spades + Jack of Diamonds) and 'Royal Marriage' (King + Queen of Trumps) after winning tricks. The game is a race to 1000 points, characterized by a unique 'Trick-and-Draw' phase where hands are constantly refilled.
Developed in France in the early 19th century from the game 'Piquet' and 'Briscan'. The name might come from the Italian 'Bazzica'.
Two players only. The standard two-handed game is played head-to-head; players cut for deal with the highest card having preference (rank order A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7). No partnerships.
64 cards. Take two 52-card decks, remove all 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s, and 6s. Combine remaining. Start with 8 cards each.
Deal 8 cards to each player (3-2-3). Turn the next card for Trump. Place the remaining deck (Talon) face down.

items.text: Rubicon Bezique: 4 Decks (128 cards). Game is not played to a score but for total points over 4 deals.
